2.text: The combination-garment (see Plate XXIII, Fig. 2; also Fig. 177) consists

3.text: of a bodice, large at the shoulders, but rather close-fitting at the waist, and

4.text: passing into baggy trousers that reach a little below the knees. The neck of

5.text: the bodice is cut quite low both front and back, especially for younger women.

6.text: To keep off the cold it is bordered with a double or even a triple row of

7.text: trimming of the thick fur of the dog, fox, or wolf. On the suits of young

8.text: women these strips of fur are of different hues, contrasting strikingly with

9.text: each other. Of course this does not prevent the cold winds of the tundra

10.text: from penetrating under the bodice. The sleeves are very full, and so long

11.text: that they interfere with the work of the woman. Moreover, they are not

12.text: gathered in at the opening. On account of these sleeves, the woman, when

13.text: occupied in several branches of work, has to thrust her right arm and shoulder

14.text: out of the bodice, while the sleeve is left dangling down the back. This

15.text: attitude, with half of the bust bare, is one of the most typical for Chukchee

16.text: women (see Plate XXVII, Fig. 3). The front of the garment opens a short distance

17.text: down from the neck, and may be fastened with curried leather bands attached

18.text: to both edges. The garment is without any opening to allow the women to

19.text: attend to the requirements of nature. For such purposes the body must be

20.text: entirely removed, allowing the garment to fall down on the knees. In winter

21.text: the women then cover their naked bodies with overcoats thrown over their

22.text: shoulders, but in summer they may be seen about the camps quite uncovered.
22.note: A small comma-shaped ink speck sits just right of "they", separated from the letter and below cap-height. Grammatically no comma belongs there ("they may be seen" is the clause). Read as a blot, not a compositor's mark; keyed as nothing per keying_spec.md §2.14 ("never a mark of punctuation, which is a blot and is keyed as nothing").
